samples.question: The picture shows one thin wire lying on a plain background. The wire is folded into nine straight runs that alternate between horizontal and vertical, so it turns a right angle between one run and the next, and both of its ends are bare. Five identical small solid square beads sit on the wire; they are all the same size and the same colour, and each one is threaded on the wire rather than resting beside it. Number the beads along the wire, starting from whichever of the two bare ends lies further to the left: the bead met first is the first bead, the next one met is the second bead, and so on up to the fifth bead. The travelled distance from a bead to an end is how far you walk along the wire itself, following every bend, to get from that bead to that end; it is not the straight-line distance across the page, and horizontal and vertical travel count in the same units. Exactly one bead has the same travelled distance to the left-hand end as to the right-hand end, so it cuts the wire into two halves of equal travel; every other bead is clearly nearer one end than the other along the wire. That balanced bead is never the first or the fifth bead. The wire's colour, the page colour, how long any run is, where the wire sits on the page, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which bead has equal travelled distance along the wire to each of the two ends? Answer with one of: second, third, fourth.
